title: Class 6 Science · Ch 3 Worksheet B · Balanced Diet & Tests
instructions: Practise the idea of a balanced diet and the simple food tests.

questions.question: Iodine solution turns blue-black on a food that contains
questions.explanation: The iodine test turns blue-black with starch.

questions.question: Rubbing a food on plain paper and seeing an oily mark suggests the food has
questions.explanation: Fat leaves an oily mark on paper.

questions.question: A diet that has all food groups in suitable amounts is called a _____ diet.
questions.explanation: A balanced diet has every nutrient in the right amount.

questions.question: Eating only sugary biscuits all day is a balanced diet.
questions.explanation: Sugary biscuits give carbs and fat but no protein, vitamins, or fibre.

questions.question: Adding lemon to a meal helps the body absorb iron.
questions.explanation: Vitamin C in lemon enhances iron absorption.

questions.question: Why is breakfast important for school children?
questions.answer: Breakfast supplies energy and concentration after the long overnight gap. Skipping it leaves children weak, distracted, and tempted to overeat later.

questions.question: You want to test whether a slice of bread contains starch. Explain how.
questions.answer: Place a small piece of bread on a plate. Add 1-2 drops of iodine solution. If it turns blue-black, it contains starch. (Bread does — wheat is high in starch.)

questions.question: Two children eat the same amount of rice. One also eats dal, vegetables, and milk. Compare the long-term effects on their health.
questions.answer: The child eating only rice gets energy but lacks proteins, vitamins, minerals, fibre — over time growth is slower, falling sick is easier, and tiredness is common. The second child gets all major nutrients, supporting growth, immunity, and energy. Variety matters more than quantity.
